comparator.name: Data Science and Society
comparator.sourceNotes: This example follows the AI and Society specialization. It includes a field project in the second year and a 30 EC minor and 15 EC thesis in the third year.
components: Introduction to Data Science and Society
Introduces data science and its social context.
Introduces programming for working with data.
Examines relationships between science, technology and society.
Governance and Regulation of Innovation I: Introduction
Introduces governance and regulation of innovation.
Introduces statistical learning and machine learning.
Develops visual ways to communicate data.
Human Rights in the Digital Age I: Human Dignity
Examines human dignity and rights in digital settings.
Continues the study of science, technology and society.
Draws conclusions from data using statistical inference.
Data Science I: Databases and Data Sources
Data Science II: Big Data Analytics
Studies the analysis of large datasets.
Governance and Regulation of Innovation II: Responsibility
Data Science III: Using Data to Solve Social Problems
Uses data to investigate social problems.
Data Science IV: Using Data to Solve Business Problems
Uses data to investigate business problems.
Human Rights in the Digital Age II: Reconsidering Impact
Examines how digital systems affect rights.
Studies how visual choices shape the interpretation of data.
Governance and Regulation of Innovation III: Sustainability
Develops a data project with researchers and a public or private organization.
Introduces deep learning architectures and workflows.
Examines the ethical and political dimensions of AI.
Applies deep learning to problems such as language modeling.
Studies rules and approaches for governing AI.
Develops research design and project planning.
Studies how people interact with machines.

routeSelection.basis: The degree offers two specializations. AI and Society is listed first in the official degree information and is the example shown. The Cognitive Technology specialization remains a distinct official direction.

alternatives.label: Data science, AI and society
alternatives.labelReason: The title reflects the subjects and methods studied in the plan.
alternatives.concept: Use programming, databases and machine learning to study social and organizational questions. Examine the effects of AI on fairness, privacy and human rights, and use research methods to evaluate evidence.
progression: Programming, data science, research methods and mathematics precede predictive modeling, databases, organizational research and advanced AI. Sociology and AI ethics develop alongside human rights and applied digital strategy.

alternatives.label: Cognition, data science and AI
alternatives.labelReason: The title reflects the subjects and methods studied in the plan.
alternatives.concept: Study how people and machines interpret information. Connect perception, language and cognition with computer vision and machine learning, and learn to design and evaluate research on human behavior.
progression: Brain and behavior precedes psycholinguistics. Neurobiology and perception build toward higher cognitive functions. Programming, data science and mathematics prepare students for machine learning, advanced algorithms and computer vision.
alternatives.distinctness: 13 courses and 97.5 EC differ each way. The cognitive plan adds brain science, language, perception, computer vision and behavioral research. The other plan emphasizes ethics, rights, digital strategy and social inquiry.

blocks: Both develop programming skills. UCR focuses on Python and computational problem-solving.
Both study how data are organized and retrieved. UCR focuses on relational modeling and SQL.
Both use visualizations to explore and communicate data. UCR also teaches data cleaning and analysis.
Both use statistical and machine learning methods for prediction and model evaluation.
Both develop neural network methods, from foundational architectures to more advanced applications.
Both develop probability and statistical inference.
Groningen combines data science and its social context in one introductory course.
Groningen has a dedicated big data analytics course. UCR develops advanced analysis through machine learning and neural networks.
Groningen studies the rhetoric of data graphics. UCR develops visual analysis and data visualization in separate settings.
Groningen has a dedicated advanced programming course. UCR develops programming through several computational courses.
Both examine foundations of human rights. UCR covers general rights theory and legal protections.
Both examine AI ethics and public consequences, including fairness, privacy and accountability.
Both apply research and data analysis to business questions. UCR focuses on customers and markets.
Groningen studies science and technology as social practices. UCR addresses social institutions and technology across courses.
Groningen continues its science and technology studies sequence.
Groningen has a dedicated course on governance of innovation.
Groningen studies responsibility in innovation. UCR addresses related questions through AI ethics and organizational study.
Groningen applies human rights to digital impacts in a second dedicated course.
Groningen applies data science directly to social problems. UCR develops data analysis and social research through separate courses.
Groningen studies sustainability in its innovation-governance sequence.
Groningen studies AI regulation as a dedicated subject.
Groningen uses a dedicated simulation exercise. UCR applies computational models to decision problems.
Groningen applies advanced AI to problems such as language modeling. UCR also studies text classification and generation in its neural networks course.
Groningen has a dedicated human–machine interaction course. UCR studies related questions through cognition, perception and AI.
Both develop research design. UCR includes measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments.
Groningen requires a 10 EC field project.
Groningen reserves 30 EC for an approved minor.
Groningen requires a 15 EC thesis. UCR’s optional research element is outside the scheduled degree.

selection.assessment: The closest plan connects technical data work with ethics, rights, governance and applications. The Cognitive Technology specialization supports a second, distinct direction. Business data and visual communication are integrated components of the common curriculum and are covered within the selected directions.

core: Programming, databases, statistics, visualisation and machine learning
Societal, ethical and human-rights consequences of datafication
Governance, law, policy and sustainability for data and AI
Applied data projects, organisations and public communication
Responsible AI methods, research design and professional practice
adjacent: Cognitive technology, computer vision, speech and human-data interaction
questions: How can data and AI address societal and organisational problems?
How should data systems be governed to protect dignity, privacy and fairness?
How can technical evidence be visualised and communicated for responsible decisions?

notes.text: Groningen combines data science with dedicated courses in digital rights, innovation governance and human–machine interaction. It also requires a field project and a thesis.
Groningen allocates 5 EC to research design and project management and 15 EC to the thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: Study programming, statistics and AI alongside questions about rights, governance and society. Groningen teaches this degree in English at Campus Fryslân in Leeuwarden.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The Groningen example follows AI and Society. The UCR options emphasize social applications and ethics, or cognition and the ways people and machines interpret information.
